facts.fact: Internet Society Pulse, from PeeringDB data last updated January 2026, lists BENIN-IX in Cotonou with 4 member networks (ISOCEL SA, SBIN, PCH AS3856, PCH AS42), 12 Gbps cumulative port capacity and 1 of 4 members peering at the route server.

Internet Society Pulse (PeeringDB, January 2026) shows BENIN-IX in Cotonou with 2 of its 4 members registered in the United States (PCH AS3856 and PCH AS42) and 2 in Benin, so networks from another country are members at an exchange in Benin.

The Internet Society says the technical community completed deployment of the Cotonou Internet Exchange (COTIX) at the end of 2024, launching with four members, with Internet Society training of local engineers in IXP operations and BGP.

facts.fact: BENINIX, Benin's exchange point in Cotonou, was in service in 2021 with 6 networks connected (founded by operators and ISPs, run as an association hosted at the incumbent's premises with a backup at the ACE cable landing site), per the Internet Society Benin chapter's June 2023 study, which also reports it is underfunded and its equipment more than ten years old.

Traffic: 859 Mbps (peak) at BENINIX on 2021, against 10,000 Mbps at Burkina Faso's BFIX, per the Internet Society Benin chapter's June 2023 study citing ISOC's 2021 report (Kende); the year of the peak is given, not the day.
